P1.title: Three Ways Up
P1.prompt: How will our satellite get to space? Pick a rocket. Each one has a price, a risk and an orbit.

choices.label: Rideshare rocket
choices.detail: Cheap (0.30 M) and 95% safe. But the orbit is fixed at 500 km.

choices.label: Dedicated rocket
choices.detail: 1.2 M and 92% safe. We pick the orbit. Costs half our money!

choices.label: Launch from the space station
choices.detail: Cheap. Flies low (400 km). Air drag pulls it down in about 1 year.

P1.hint: Slide the marker into the green zone: our weight plus 10% spare, under the limit.
P1.clue: COST at the top must stay under 2.5 M. A cheap rocket saves money.

P2.title: Orbit Ring
P2.prompt: Which orbit do we want? A higher orbit lasts longer. A lower orbit is easier to reach.

choices.label: 500 km up
choices.detail: Lasts about 5 years. The sun hits at the same angle every time.

choices.label: 600 km up
choices.detail: Lasts 20+ years, but the rocket can only lift 14 kg.

P2.clue: Only the dedicated rocket lets us choose. Other rockets pick the orbit for us.

P3.title: Surprise Jar
P3.prompt: Surprises always cost money. Should we keep some safe cash in the jar?

choices.label: Keep 0.10 M in the jar
choices.detail: Safe. If our money is cut, we do not lose a part.

choices.label: Spend it all
choices.detail: A bit more science now. But no safety money if things go wrong.

P3.clue: Look at COST at the top. We must stay under 2.5 M, jar money included.

E1.title: The Frame
E1.prompt: Pick the box for our satellite. A bigger box holds more, but it costs more.

choices.label: 6U box
choices.detail: Holds 12 kg. Costs 0.7 M. Fits the camera and a few extras.

choices.label: 3U box
choices.detail: Holds only 4 kg. Costs 0.4 M. Too small for our camera!

choices.label: 12U box
choices.detail: Holds 24 kg. Costs 1.2 M. Lots of room, but very expensive.

E1.clue: Watch MASS and COST at the top. Our camera needs a big enough box.

E2.title: Sun Test
E2.prompt: Solar panels turn sunlight into power. Which panels do we use?

choices.label: Fold-out panels
choices.detail: Make 35 W. Heavier (1 kg), 0.15 M. They also charge the battery.

choices.label: Panels on the body
choices.detail: Make only 12 W. Light and cheap, but too weak for the whole satellite.

E2.clue: POWER at the top: used / made. Made must be 1.6 times used or more.

E3.title: The Dark Box
E3.prompt: At night the satellite sits in Earth's shadow for 35 minutes. The battery must keep it alive.

choices.label: Small battery (40 Wh)
choices.detail: Gives about 20 W at night. Light: 0.5 kg.

choices.label: Big battery (80 Wh)
choices.detail: Gives about 41 W at night. Safer, but 0.5 kg heavier.

E3.hint: Keep the heater and beacon on. Turn off big loads to save battery.
E3.clue: Night power from the battery must be more than the POWER used.

E4.title: Thruster Shelf
E4.prompt: Space has junk in it. Thrusters let the satellite move away from danger.

choices.label: No thrusters
choices.detail: Lighter and cheaper. If junk comes close, we can only hope.

choices.label: Small thrusters
choices.detail: Cost 0.1 M and 0.4 kg. Dodge junk and live longer.

E4.clue: A satellite with thrusters can dodge space junk later in the game.

E5.title: Weigh-In
E5.prompt: Time to weigh the satellite. Real parts always weigh more than the drawing says. How much spare room do we keep?

choices.label: Keep 10% spare
choices.detail: Safe. Parts often weigh more than planned.

choices.label: Trim the brackets
choices.detail: Pay 0.03 M to save 0.2 kg. Keep the 10% spare too.

choices.label: Squeeze to the limit
choices.detail: No spare room and 3 months late. The launch is riskier.

E5.clue: MASS plus 10% spare must stay under the limit at the top.

C1.title: Radio Bench
C1.prompt: The radio sends our photos to Earth. A faster radio sends more, but uses more power.

choices.label: X-band radio
choices.detail: Fast (100 Mbps). Uses 20 W and 0.9 kg. Good for our camera.

choices.label: S-band radio
choices.detail: Very slow (2 Mbps). Uses 5 W. Works in rain, but too slow for us.

choices.label: Ka-band radio
choices.detail: Super fast (400 Mbps). Uses 30 W. Heavy rain blocks it.

C1.clue: DATA at the top must be 70% or more. A slow radio cannot send all the photos.

C2.title: Wall Map
C2.prompt: The satellite only sees our dish for a few minutes each day. Use one dish or rent many?

choices.label: One dish in Kuching
choices.detail: About 32 minutes a day. Cheap (0.04 M).

choices.label: Rent a dish network
choices.detail: About 112 minutes a day. Costs 0.2 M, and it is a good backup.

C2.clue: More minutes each day means more photos sent home. Watch DATA at the top.

C3.title: Pass Timeline
C3.prompt: Each pass is a short chance to talk to the satellite. Send photos on every pass, or keep one for commands?

choices.label: Send photos on every pass
choices.detail: Most photos get home. But we cannot give orders to fix problems.

choices.label: Keep one pass for commands
choices.detail: A few less photos, but we can fix faults.

C3.hint: Pick up to 3 passes. Photos sent must be 70% or more of what we take.
C3.clue: Commands are orders we send to the satellite, like "reset the camera".

S1.title: Magic Eye
S1.prompt: Our camera checks how healthy the plants are. Do we put it on board?

choices.label: Yes, fly the forest camera
choices.detail: 2.5 kg, 10 W. Makes 4 GB of photos a day. The mission needs it.

choices.label: No, skip it
choices.detail: Saves weight and money, but the mission fails.

S1.clue: Without this camera we cannot watch the forest, so the review will say NO.

S2.title: Instrument Shelf
S2.prompt: Extra tools give more science. But each one adds weight, power and more photos to send.

choices.label: Camera only
choices.detail: The safest choice. Lower science score.

choices.label: Heat camera
choices.detail: 1.2 kg, 6 W. Sees heat and fires. Sees through some clouds.

choices.label: Sharp camera (hi-res)
choices.detail: 3 kg, 7 W, 10 GB a day. Great pictures, but uses lots of power.

choices.label: Heat camera and GPS
choices.detail: 1.3 kg, 7 W. Sees heat and knows exactly where it is.

S2.hint: Tap tools to pack the bay. Keep the camera. Stay under FREE mass and power.
S2.clue: Each extra uses POWER and MASS. Stay under the numbers at the top.

S3.title: Frame the Shot
S3.prompt: Wide shots show a big area. Close-ups show clear detail. Which one do we want?

choices.label: Wide view
choices.detail: Covers more forest, but each picture is less sharp.

choices.label: Close-up detail
choices.detail: Very sharp, but 50% more data to send home.

choices.label: Look away from Sarawak
choices.detail: Pretty pictures, but outside our forest. The mission fails.

S3.clue: We must cover Sarawak. Close-ups make more data, so check DATA at the top.

S4.title: Cloud Calendar
S4.prompt: Clouds hide the forest. Do we take photos all year, or only in the clearer months?

choices.label: Clearer months only
choices.detail: Less wasted power and data. More useful pictures.

choices.label: All year
choices.detail: More photos, but many are just clouds. Uses more power.

S4.clue: Photos of clouds are wasted. Fewer photos can still mean better science.

R1.title: Power vs Science
R1.prompt: Review time. The heat camera needs 6 W and our power is almost full. Pick a fix.

choices.label: Share the power
choices.detail: Instruments take turns, so we use 1 W less.

choices.label: Run everything
choices.detail: More science, but 5 W more power used.

choices.label: Add solar panels
choices.detail: Costs 0.12 M and 0.2 kg. Makes 5 W more power.

R1.clue: Keep POWER used under 60% of POWER made, so the battery can recharge.

R2.title: Mass vs Comms
R2.prompt: Review time. The radio is heavy and we have little spare weight. Pick a fix.

choices.label: Trim the mounting plate
choices.detail: Saves 0.1 kg. Easy.

choices.label: Change nothing
choices.detail: No cost. But check the MASS number first.

choices.label: Use a bigger adapter
choices.detail: Adds 0.3 kg, 0.1 M and 1 month. The structure is stronger.

R2.clue: MASS plus 10% spare must stay under the limit at the top.

R3.title: Data vs Comms / EV7
R3.prompt: Siti wants a second camera. It makes more data than our radio can send. Aisyah, you decide.

choices.label: Say no
choices.detail: Keep the main camera. Protect the data we can send home.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.detail: More science, but 2.5 kg, 10 W and 4 GB more data a day.

choices.label: Negotiate: buy more passes
choices.detail: Pay 0.12 M for 20 more minutes a day to send more data.

R3.clue: Compare DATA and POWER at the top before you decide.

P4.title: What Comes First?
P4.prompt: We cannot have everything. What matters most to our mission?

choices.label: Safety
choices.detail: Keep extra room. The satellite is more likely to survive.

choices.label: Science
choices.detail: Go for more forest data. Safety margins get smaller.

choices.label: Cost
choices.detail: Save money for the next team. A little less science.

P4.clue: There is no wrong answer. It only changes what the team is best at.

P5.title: T-Minus
P5.prompt: Everyone says ready. This is the last call. Do we launch now, or wait one month?

choices.label: Go
choices.detail: Launch now. Anything close to a limit may cause trouble.

choices.label: Hold one month
choices.detail: Wait a month to fix the weakest spot. Costs 0.04 M.

P5.clue: Waiting costs time. But launching with a known problem can cost more.

EV8.title: Q2 - Heavy Clouds
EV8.prompt: Heavy clouds are hiding the forest. Which camera do we use?

choices.label: Switch to the heat camera
choices.detail: A heat camera sees through some clouds, if we carry one.

choices.label: Keep the normal camera
choices.detail: Clouds block the view. We lose some science.

EV8.hint: Press THERMAL before the cloud bar is full.
EV8.clue: No heat camera on board? Then switching will not help much.

EV6.title: Q3 - Station Outage
EV6.prompt: The ground dish stopped working! Send the data another way, fast.

choices.label: Use another dish
choices.detail: Send the pass to a backup dish. A dish network loses less.

choices.label: Wait for Kuching
choices.detail: Wait for the dish to work again. We lose 12% of the data.

EV6.hint: Press STATION, then BACKUP DISH, then DATA SERVER, in that order.
EV6.clue: A rented dish network is the best backup for this problem.

C4.title: Q4 - Rain at the Dish
C4.prompt: Heavy rain is over the dish. Rain weakens the radio signal.

choices.label: Slow down with the rain
choices.detail: Follow the signal and send at a slower speed.

choices.label: Keep full speed
choices.detail: Fast, but rain can ruin the data. We lose 8%.

C4.hint: Keep the needle inside the green box. Use the arrow keys (or A and D).
C4.clue: Ka-band suffers most in rain. S-band barely changes.

EV3.title: Q5 - Long Eclipse
EV3.prompt: The night is much longer this time: 55 minutes. Will the battery last?

choices.label: Turn off extra loads
choices.detail: Pause science to save battery power.

choices.label: Keep everything on
choices.detail: Uses 3 W more. A small battery may go flat.

EV3.hint: Keep the heater and beacon on. Turn off big loads to save battery.
EV3.clue: The big 80 Wh battery can survive alone. The small one needs your care.

EV9.title: Q6 - Instrument Glitch
EV9.prompt: The camera froze! Reset it in the right order.

choices.label: Reset step by step
choices.detail: Follow the right order to bring the camera back.

choices.label: Skip the reset
choices.detail: We lose science and the satellite gets weaker.

EV9.hint: Watch the pattern first. Then press the buttons in the same order.
EV9.clue: Keeping one pass for commands (Ling's choice C3) makes this problem smaller.

EV5.title: Q7 - Debris Warning
EV5.prompt: Space junk is coming! Can we steer away?

choices.label: Dodge the junk
choices.detail: Thrusters let us move away. Without them, it is a near miss.

choices.label: Keep taking photos
choices.detail: More science time, but a bigger chance of getting hit.

EV5.hint: Move with the arrow keys (or A and D). Stay away from the rocks.
EV5.clue: Only a satellite with thrusters can really dodge the junk.

EV4.title: Q8 - Battery Heating
EV4.prompt: The battery is getting too hot! Take some loads off.

choices.label: Cool it down
choices.detail: Turn off big loads so the battery can cool.

choices.label: Keep full power
choices.detail: Too much heat damages the battery and shortens its life.

EV4.hint: Turn off big loads until the load number is low. Keep heater and beacon on.
EV4.clue: A hot battery loses life. Switch off big loads to keep it safe.
